$about: Scrim's .fig importer, run on its own fixtures and on hostile inputs: the expectations a Rust port must meet.
Every value here was produced by RUNNING packages/fig-import/dist (Scrim f2b1bdb) from scripts outside the repo; nothing is hand-typed except the asserts, and those were checked against the run.

generatedBy.builders: the fixture builders and test encoder are packages/fig-import/src/__tests__/fixtures.ts and figEncoder.ts, copied verbatim (one import path changed); they reproduce tests/fixtures/fig/*.fig byte for byte

conventions.nodeAddressing: Nodes have no ids here (Scrim's are random). `path` is the tree path: '<rootIndex>:<name>' then '/<childIndex>:<name>' per level. `node` selectors in asserts are a layer name (first match in tree order) or { name, under } (the first match inside the named ancestor).
conventions.units: Numbers in style/layout are CSS px unless the value is a string with its own unit. Colours are #rrggbb when opaque, else rgba(r, g, b, a) with a rounded to 3 decimals.
conventions.figmaBox: Each node's box in Figma, relative to its top-level artboard (its transform composed through its ancestors; rotated layers as their axis-aligned bounds). Measurement only: never in the document. Instance content has no figmaBox (only the instance root).
conventions.patchOps: Scrim op names; a port need not reproduce them. One import = ONE patch = one undo step.
conventions.imagePipeline: importFig takes the host's image pipeline. stage-a and stage-b ran with one that accepts every image (src = scrim-asset:<sha256>.png); the others with one that refuses (they carry no image bytes).

zipCrc.fact: The test encoder (figEncoder.ts › zip) writes CRC-32 = 0 in every local header and central-directory entry. The one committed zipped fixture is tests/fixtures/fig/stage-a.fig; every ZIP-based security case below has CRC 0 too.
zipCrc.scrimReader: Scrim's reader (container.ts › readArchive) never reads either CRC field: CRC 0, or any wrong CRC, is accepted. It also ignores the local header's sizes and name (the central directory's are used), and data-descriptor flag bit 3 needs no handling for the same reason. Integrity rests on: the declared uncompressed size must equal the inflated length, the image entries must hash to their SHA-1 name, and the Kiwi decode must consume the data exactly.
zipCrc.figcraft: FigCraft refuses these zips ("Invalid checksum"; docs/research/figcraft-spike.md §3). A port that verifies CRCs must either accept CRC 0 for the fixtures or re-zip them with real CRCs; crc32Actual below is the value a correct writer would store.

security.name: nested instances expand exponentially
security.inputDescription: 8 masters M0..M7 on one page; each M(i) holds 4 instances of M(i+1); M7 holds one rectangle. Instances inside a master are expanded inline as detached copies, so the layers grow as 4^levels (levels 9: 203,886 layers from a 2,191-byte file in 11.6 s; each further level is about 4× the layers and 5× the time)
security.howToBuild: nestedInstances(8, 4): see gen-security.ts
